Professional Culinary Practice

More than ever, qualified restaurant managers are in high demand. Recent global disruptions have demonstrated the scarcity of skilled restaurant managers and other roles responsible for the coordination of culinary operations.

These roles require a unique combination of skills, including orchestration and innovation, teamwork and self-management, and problem solving and adaptability. On a daily basis, restaurant and kitchen managers are responsible for supervising kitchen and service personnel, developing and costing menus, and maintaining quality and safety standards.

This major integrates the theoretical and practical elements of culinary operations to acquire the required knowledge, skills, and attitudes for a successful career in today’s fast-changing, fast-paced restaurant industry. Through this major, students will progress from basic to advanced culinary skills and techniques in the French classical tradition.

Additional fees for culinary uniform apply when selecting this major.

Units: Kitchens Operations Management, Food and Beverage Service, Culinary Practice.

The Bachelor of Business - International Hotel Management enables students to become an inspiring leader in the dynamic world of hotel management. Students have the opportunity to apply communication skills, marketing knowledge and business strategies to the realities of managing a hotel or resort. The Bachelor of Business in International Hotel Management degree creates globally-focused, multi-skilled, career-ready hospitality leaders.

The following are a number of career options available to graduates:

  • Rooms Division Manager
  • Convention and Event Management
  • Sales and Marketing Manager
  • Revenue Management
  • Human Resources Management
  • Recruitment Manager

77ob:
The course is called ‘Applied Hospitality Management’ because its primary aim is to equip students for a rewarding career in a range of hospitality roles, to be work-ready even prior to graduation and to set them on the path to success. The curriculum is tightly integrated to ensure that graduates share a common skillset and attributes that prepare them for senior hospitality management roles.

Combining industry-led experience with cutting-edge teaching, the Master of Applied Hospitality Management (MAHM) focuses on the skills, understanding and knowledge to be a leader in hospitality management.

Emphasis is placed on acquiring the ‘soft’ as well as technical skills required to manage a modern hospitality business, from operations to business continuity management. Service quality management and revenue management are integral to the course, along with business planning, both of which set the foundations for an entrepreneurial and creative mindset that differentiates the Le Cordon Bleu MAHM from others that are less focused on the customer experience and problem-solving.
9603:
The Master of Applied Supply Chain Management (CRICOS Code: 113968D) is a postgraduate program designed to develop advanced knowledge and practical skills in managing supply chains across global industries.

The program focuses on key areas such as logistics, procurement, operations management, inventory control, and supply chain strategy. Students learn how to design, manage, and optimize supply chains to improve efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance organizational performance.

The curriculum emphasizes data-driven decision-making, analytical tools, and the use of technology in modern supply chain operations. Students also explore topics such as global trade, risk management, sustainability, and supply chain innovation.

Through case studies, simulations, and applied projects, students gain practical experience in solving real-world supply chain challenges. The program also develops essential skills in problem-solving, strategic thinking, and leadership.

Graduates are prepared for roles such as supply chain manager, logistics manager, procurement specialist, operations manager, and business analyst in a wide range of industries including manufacturing, retail, transportation, and e-commerce.

Overall, this program is ideal for individuals seeking to build or advance a career in supply chain management, with a strong focus on practical application, global perspective, and industry-relevant skills.
9602:
The Master of Professional Accounting (CRICOS Code: 113965G) is a postgraduate program designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills required for careers in accounting, finance, and related business fields.

The program covers core areas of accounting such as financial accounting, management accounting, auditing, taxation, and business law, along with supporting subjects in economics, finance, and business analytics. It is designed to develop both technical accounting expertise and practical business skills.

Students learn how to analyze financial information, prepare reports, ensure regulatory compliance, and support organizational decision-making. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, and ethical practices, which are essential in the accounting profession.

Many programs also align with the academic requirements for professional accounting bodies such as CPA Australia, CA ANZ (Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand), and ACCA, helping graduates work toward professional certification.

Through case studies and applied learning, students gain practical experience relevant to real-world accounting and business environments.

Graduates are prepared for roles such as accountant, auditor, tax consultant, financial analyst, and management accountant across various industries.

Overall, this program is ideal for individuals seeking to build a strong foundation in professional accounting and advance their career in finance and business.
